newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir repair job put off, may delay new crew launch.
newsitem.headline: Mir repair job put off, may delay new crew launch.

text.p: Risky repairs on the crippled Mir space station, due to have been performed later this week, have been postponed, Interfax news agency quoted mission director Viktor Blagov as saying on Tuesday.
Earlier, a training session scheduled for Tuesday was postponed to give the crew, whose commander has fallen ill, more time to rest.

"The sortie of the Russian cosmonauts into the Spektr module to repair the electrical system of the Russian orbital complex, planned for the night of July 19, is postponed to a later date," Interfax said, quoting Blagov.
A representative of the U.S. NASA space agency told Reuters at Russian Mission Control near Moscow the postponement might also delay the launch of a spacecraft with a relief crew.
"It looks like the repairs sortie is postponed -- and this fact may affect the date of the launch of a fresh crew," said the NASA representative, who declined to be named.
The new three-man Russian-French crew was due to take off for Mir on August 5.
The repair work is intended to restore power lost last month after Mir's collision with a cargo craft on June 25, the worst accident in the station's 11 years in space.
A Russian space official, who also declined to be named, said the postponement was not necessarily linked with the health of the cosmonauts.
"It means that they are not quite ready for the repairs," he told Reuters.

A special committee of doctors was to meet during the day to discuss the health of Mir commander Vasily Tsibliyev. He told Mission Control on Monday he had developed cardiovascular health problems, but the exact nature of his illness was not clear.

Mission Control had said earlier the crew would sleep until midday (0800 GMT) on Tuesday to help shift their sleep cycle before doing the repairs. They were scheduled for the Moscow night of Thursday to Friday or Friday to Saturday.
The fresh crew is rehearsing on Earth, getting ready to seal the punctured body of the Spektr module. The crew on board is only to repair the power supply.
